Economics as a Science.text: Which of the following is the best definition of economics?
options: The study of how firms advertise their products
The study of how government controls the production of goods
The study of how money is printed and circulated
The study of how man allocates scarce resources among competing unlimited wants
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: The study of how man allocates scarce resources among competing unlimited wants

Economics as a Science.text: Economics is regarded as a science mainly because it __________.
options: deals only with money and banking
uses systematic methods of observation, hypothesis and testing to study economic behaviour
cannot be studied without a laboratory
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: uses systematic methods of observation, hypothesis and testing to study economic behaviour

Economics as a Science.text: In economics, a want may be defined as __________.
options: any good that is free of charge
the amount of money a person earns monthly
the total output of a country in a year
a desire for a good or service which gives satisfaction when met
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: a desire for a good or service which gives satisfaction when met

Economics as a Science.text: One key characteristic of human wants that gives rise to the economic problem is that they are __________.
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: unlimited and recurring

Economics as a Science.text: Scarcity in economics refers to __________.
options: the total absence of any resource
the deliberate withholding of goods by producers
a temporary shortage caused by strikes
a situation where resources are insufficient to satisfy all human wants
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: a situation where resources are insufficient to satisfy all human wants

Economics as a Science.text: The fundamental economic problem faced by all societies, rich or poor, is __________.
options: scarcity of resources relative to unlimited wants
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: scarcity of resources relative to unlimited wants

Economics as a Science.text: Because resources are scarce, individuals and societies are forced to make __________.
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: choices

Economics as a Science.text: A scale of preference can best be described as __________.
options: an arrangement of wants in order of their importance so that the most pressing want is satisfied first
a list of goods a consumer refuses to buy
a record of a firm's total sales for the year
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: an arrangement of wants in order of their importance so that the most pressing want is satisfied first

Economics as a Science.text: The main purpose of drawing up a scale of preference is to __________.
options: help in the rational allocation of scarce resources among competing wants
guarantee that all wants will eventually be satisfied
increase the total number of wants a person has
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: help in the rational allocation of scarce resources among competing wants

Economics as a Science.text: On a consumer's scale of preference, the want placed first is usually the one that is __________.
options: most pressing and given top priority
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: most pressing and given top priority

Economics as a Science.text: Opportunity cost is best defined as __________.
options: the total money spent on a good
the value of the next best alternative forgone when a choice is made
the price tag placed on a good by the government
the cost of transporting goods to the market
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: the value of the next best alternative forgone when a choice is made

Economics as a Science.text: Opportunity cost is also commonly referred to as the __________.
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: real cost

Economics as a Science.text: A farmer has enough land to plant either yam or maize but not both. If he chooses to plant yam, the opportunity cost of his decision is __________.
options: the fertilizer applied to the yam
the labour used to plant the yam
the maize he could have planted instead
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: the maize he could have planted instead

Economics as a Science.text: A student has ₦2,000 and can either buy a textbook or a pair of shoes, each costing ₦2,000. If she buys the textbook, her opportunity cost is __________.
options: nothing, since she made a rational choice
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: the pair of shoes forgone

Economics as a Science.text: An economic agent is said to be rational when he __________.
options: spends all his income on luxury goods
always follows the decisions of the government
aims to maximize satisfaction or benefit while minimizing cost or sacrifice
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: aims to maximize satisfaction or benefit while minimizing cost or sacrifice

Economics as a Science.text: The assumption that consumers and producers always act in their own best self-interest to maximize gain is known as the assumption of __________.
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: the economic man (rationality)

Economics as a Science.text: Production, in economics, refers to __________.
options: only the manufacturing of physical goods in a factory
the creation of goods and services that satisfy human wants, including the addition of utility
the storage of finished goods in a warehouse
the buying and selling of shares on the stock exchange
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: the creation of goods and services that satisfy human wants, including the addition of utility

Economics as a Science.text: Which of the following is NOT one of the traditional factors of production?
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: Advertising

Economics as a Science.text: The reward paid to the factor of production called land is __________.
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: rent

Economics as a Science.text: Wages are the reward that accrues to which factor of production?
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: Labour

Economics as a Science.text: Interest, as a factor reward, is paid to the owners of __________.
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: capital

Economics as a Science.text: The entrepreneur, as a factor of production, is rewarded with __________.
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: profit

Economics as a Science.text: In economics, distribution refers to __________.
options: the sharing of the national income among the various factors of production
the transportation of goods from farm to market only
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: the sharing of the national income among the various factors of production

Economics as a Science.text: Consumption in economics means __________.
options: the storage of goods for future sale
the direct use of goods and services to satisfy human wants
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: the direct use of goods and services to satisfy human wants

Economics as a Science.text: "What to produce?" as one of the basic economic problems, is concerned with __________.
options: deciding who should own the factories
deciding the exchange rate of the currency
deciding which goods and services, and in what quantities, should be produced with scarce resources
deciding the interest rate charged by banks
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: deciding which goods and services, and in what quantities, should be produced with scarce resources

Economics as a Science.text: The basic economic question of "how to produce?" deals mainly with __________.
options: choosing the combination of resources and techniques used in production
deciding the colour of the packaging
deciding the price of the final good
deciding which country to export to
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: choosing the combination of resources and techniques used in production

Economics as a Science.text: "For whom to produce?" is a basic economic problem that addresses __________.
options: how the output produced is to be distributed or shared among members of society
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: how the output produced is to be distributed or shared among members of society

Economics as a Science.text: The underlying cause of all three basic economic problems (what, how, and for whom to produce) is __________.
options: scarcity of resources relative to unlimited wants
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: scarcity of resources relative to unlimited wants

Economics as a Science.text: Resource efficiency in economics is achieved when __________.
options: scarce resources are used in a way that maximizes output or satisfaction with minimum waste
resources are left idle to prevent wastage
resources are exported rather than used locally
all resources are owned by the government
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: scarce resources are used in a way that maximizes output or satisfaction with minimum waste

Economics as a Science.text: An economy is said to be operating at full and efficient use of its resources when __________.
options: prices are fixed by the government
there is no unemployment of resources and output cannot be increased without sacrificing another good
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: there is no unemployment of resources and output cannot be increased without sacrificing another good

Economics as a Science.text: The Production Possibility Frontier (PPF) may be defined as a curve that shows __________.
options: the various maximum combinations of two goods that can be produced with given resources and technology
the demand for a good at different prices
the rate of inflation over several years
the total population of a country over time
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: the various maximum combinations of two goods that can be produced with given resources and technology

Economics as a Science.text: The Production Possibility Curve is typically drawn concave to the origin because __________.
options: resources are perfectly substitutable between the two goods
prices of both goods always rise together
population grows at a constant rate
opportunity cost increases as more of one good is produced at the expense of the other
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: opportunity cost increases as more of one good is produced at the expense of the other

Economics as a Science.text: A point lying exactly on the Production Possibility Curve represents __________.
options: full and efficient utilization of available resources
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: full and efficient utilization of available resources

Economics as a Science.text: A point lying inside (below) the Production Possibility Curve indicates that __________.
options: resources are being fully and efficiently utilized
the good on the vertical axis has become a free good
the economy has achieved maximum growth
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: resources are underutilized or unemployed

Economics as a Science.text: A point lying outside the Production Possibility Curve represents a combination of output that is __________.
options: currently attainable with existing resources and technology
the same as a point on the curve
always more efficient than points on the curve
unattainable with the current level of resources and technology
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: unattainable with the current level of resources and technology

Economics as a Science.text: Movement from one point to another along a given Production Possibility Curve illustrates __________.
options: the opportunity cost of producing more of one good in terms of the other good forgone
a fall in the price level
an increase in total resources available
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: the opportunity cost of producing more of one good in terms of the other good forgone

Economics as a Science.text: An outward shift of the entire Production Possibility Curve is most likely caused by __________.
options: improved technology or an increase in the quantity/quality of resources
a natural disaster that destroys capital
a fall in the labour force
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: improved technology or an increase in the quantity/quality of resources

Economics as a Science.text: One of the basic assumptions underlying the standard Production Possibility Curve is that __________.
options: an unlimited quantity of resources is available
resources and technology are fixed while only two goods are considered
only one good can ever be produced
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: resources and technology are fixed while only two goods are considered

Economics as a Science.text: If a Production Possibility Curve is drawn as a straight line rather than a curve, this implies that __________.
options: opportunity cost increases as production of one good rises
only one good is being produced
opportunity cost remains constant regardless of the combination produced
resources cannot be transferred between the two goods at all
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: opportunity cost remains constant regardless of the combination produced

Economics as a Science.text: The branch of economics that studies individual units such as households, firms, and prices of specific goods is called __________.
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: microeconomics

Economics as a Science.text: The branch of economics that studies the economy as a whole, dealing with aggregates such as national income and general price level, is called __________.
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: macroeconomics

Economics as a Science.text: Economics is best described as a social science because it __________.
options: deals only with the physical environment
is not concerned with human behaviour at all
studies human behaviour in relation to the use of scarce resources within society
studies the behaviour of chemical substances
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: studies human behaviour in relation to the use of scarce resources within society

Economics as a Science.text: A free good, as distinct from an economic good, is one that __________.
options: is always more expensive than an economic good
is available in unlimited supply relative to demand and therefore has no price
can only be obtained through government allocation
is scarce and commands a price
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: is available in unlimited supply relative to demand and therefore has no price

Economics as a Science.text: An economic good is one that __________.
options: is unlimited in supply and has no opportunity cost
is scarce relative to demand, has an opportunity cost, and commands a price
is produced only by the government
Economics as a Science.correct_answer: is scarce relative to demand, has an opportunity cost, and commands a price

Economic Systems.text: An economic system may be defined as __________.
options: the exchange rate policy of a central bank
the set of institutions and arrangements a society uses to answer the basic economic questions of what, how, and for whom to produce
a list of goods produced by the government alone
the total amount of money in circulation in a country
Economic Systems.correct_answer: the set of institutions and arrangements a society uses to answer the basic economic questions of what, how, and for whom to produce

Economic Systems.text: Capitalism, also called the free enterprise economy, is an economic system characterized mainly by __________.
options: state ownership of all factors of production
private ownership of the means of production and reliance on the price mechanism
equal distribution of income by law
Economic Systems.correct_answer: private ownership of the means of production and reliance on the price mechanism

Economic Systems.text: Which of the following is a key feature of the capitalist economic system?
options: Central planning of all production decisions by the state
Fixed prices set only by government decree
Freedom of individuals to own private property and engage in business for profit
Economic Systems.correct_answer: Freedom of individuals to own private property and engage in business for profit

Economic Systems.text: One major merit of the capitalist (free enterprise) economic system is that __________.
options: it guarantees equal income for everyone
competition and the profit motive tend to encourage efficiency and innovation
the government controls all prices directly
Economic Systems.correct_answer: competition and the profit motive tend to encourage efficiency and innovation

Economic Systems.text: A major demerit commonly associated with the capitalist economic system is __________.
options: excessive government bureaucracy in all production decisions
wide inequality in the distribution of income and wealth
Economic Systems.correct_answer: wide inequality in the distribution of income and wealth

Economic Systems.text: A socialist (command) economy is one in which __________.
options: private individuals own all major industries
the means of production are largely owned and controlled by the state, which also plans economic activity
prices are determined solely by the interaction of private buyers and sellers
there is no government involvement in the economy whatsoever
Economic Systems.correct_answer: the means of production are largely owned and controlled by the state, which also plans economic activity

Economic Systems.text: A distinguishing feature of a centrally planned economic system is __________.
options: unrestricted private ownership of large industries
reliance on the price mechanism alone to allocate resources
the total absence of production targets
the existence of a central planning authority that decides what, how, and for whom to produce
Economic Systems.correct_answer: the existence of a central planning authority that decides what, how, and for whom to produce

Economic Systems.text: One merit often claimed for a socialist economic system is that it __________.
options: always produces goods more efficiently than any other system
tends to reduce inequality in the distribution of income and wealth
gives individuals unrestricted freedom to own large businesses
Economic Systems.correct_answer: tends to reduce inequality in the distribution of income and wealth

Economic Systems.text: A commonly cited demerit of the socialist (command) economic system is that it may lead to __________.
options: inefficiency and lack of individual initiative due to the absence of the profit motive
total absence of a planning authority
Economic Systems.correct_answer: inefficiency and lack of individual initiative due to the absence of the profit motive

Economic Systems.text: A mixed economic system can best be described as one in which __________.
options: only foreign investors are permitted to own businesses
both the private sector and the public sector participate in economic activities
only the government undertakes economic activities
there is no market for goods and services
Economic Systems.correct_answer: both the private sector and the public sector participate in economic activities

Economic Systems.text: A key feature of a mixed economy is __________.
options: the total absence of government regulation
the coexistence of private enterprise with government ownership and regulation of certain sectors
the complete abolition of private property
prices fixed entirely by a central planning board
Economic Systems.correct_answer: the coexistence of private enterprise with government ownership and regulation of certain sectors

Economic Systems.text: Nigeria's economic system is generally classified as __________.
options: a pure capitalist economy with no government involvement
a mixed economy, combining private enterprise with government participation
Economic Systems.correct_answer: a mixed economy, combining private enterprise with government participation

Economic Systems.text: Under a capitalist economy, the question of "what to produce" is mainly answered by __________.
options: consumer demand and the price mechanism (consumer sovereignty)
Economic Systems.correct_answer: consumer demand and the price mechanism (consumer sovereignty)

Economic Systems.text: Under a socialist economy, the question of "what to produce" is mainly decided by __________.
options: the central planning authority of the state
the price mechanism operating freely in the market
Economic Systems.correct_answer: the central planning authority of the state

Economic Systems.text: Under the capitalist system, the question of "how to produce" is typically determined by __________.
options: producers seeking the least-cost, most profitable method of production
Economic Systems.correct_answer: producers seeking the least-cost, most profitable method of production

Economic Systems.text: Under a socialist economy, the question of "for whom to produce" is generally decided by __________.
options: individual consumers bidding in a free market
the state or planning authority, often based on perceived need
Economic Systems.correct_answer: the state or planning authority, often based on perceived need

Economic Systems.text: The price mechanism refers to __________.
options: a government decree fixing all prices
the system by which the forces of demand and supply interact to determine prices and allocate resources
a tax imposed on imported goods
Economic Systems.correct_answer: the system by which the forces of demand and supply interact to determine prices and allocate resources

Economic Systems.text: The concept of the "invisible hand," associated with Adam Smith, describes how __________.
options: central banks control the money supply
government planning guides all economic decisions
trade unions negotiate wages on behalf of workers
individuals pursuing their own self-interest in a free market unintentionally promote the overall good of society
Economic Systems.correct_answer: individuals pursuing their own self-interest in a free market unintentionally promote the overall good of society

Economic Systems.text: Which of the following terms is used interchangeably with capitalism?
Economic Systems.correct_answer: Free market/free enterprise economy

Economic Systems.text: Which of the following terms is used interchangeably with socialism?
Economic Systems.correct_answer: Command/centrally planned economy

Economic Systems.text: One merit of a mixed economic system is that __________.
options: it combines the efficiency of private enterprise with government intervention to correct market failures and promote welfare
it prevents any form of private business activity
it guarantees there will never be unemployment
it removes the price mechanism completely
Economic Systems.correct_answer: it combines the efficiency of private enterprise with government intervention to correct market failures and promote welfare

Economic Systems.text: A possible demerit of a mixed economic system is that __________.
options: it always leads to perfect equality of income
it can lead to conflict or inefficiency arising from the dual control of the private and public sectors
there is no role for government at all
Economic Systems.correct_answer: it can lead to conflict or inefficiency arising from the dual control of the private and public sectors

Economic Systems.text: Privatization refers to the __________.
options: transfer of ownership or control of state-owned enterprises to private individuals or organizations
process by which government takes over privately owned companies
removal of all taxes on private businesses
printing of new currency by the central bank
Economic Systems.correct_answer: transfer of ownership or control of state-owned enterprises to private individuals or organizations

Economic Systems.text: One major reason governments, including Nigeria's, embark on privatization of public enterprises is to __________.
options: improve efficiency, reduce the financial burden on government, and attract private investment
Economic Systems.correct_answer: improve efficiency, reduce the financial burden on government, and attract private investment

Economic Systems.text: Deregulation, as used in economic policy, refers to __________.
options: the reduction or removal of government rules and controls governing an industry to allow market forces to operate more freely
the introduction of new and stricter government controls on an industry
the fixing of prices by government decree
Economic Systems.correct_answer: the reduction or removal of government rules and controls governing an industry to allow market forces to operate more freely

Economic Systems.text: An example of deregulation in the Nigerian economy is __________.
options: the liberalization of the telecommunications sector, which allowed private operators to compete with the former state monopoly
the banning of private telecommunications companies
the creation of a new state-owned airline
the fixing of all retail prices by law
Economic Systems.correct_answer: the liberalization of the telecommunications sector, which allowed private operators to compete with the former state monopoly

Economic Systems.text: Economic reform generally refers to __________.
options: the process of printing more currency notes
a reduction in the population of a country
the abolition of all forms of taxation
deliberate policy changes aimed at improving the structure, efficiency, and performance of an economy
Economic Systems.correct_answer: deliberate policy changes aimed at improving the structure, efficiency, and performance of an economy

Economic Systems.text: The Nigerian banking sector consolidation of 2004/2005 mainly involved __________.
options: reducing the minimum capital requirement for banks
raising the minimum capital base of banks and encouraging mergers to create fewer, stronger banks
banning foreign banks from operating in Nigeria
Economic Systems.correct_answer: raising the minimum capital base of banks and encouraging mergers to create fewer, stronger banks

Economic Systems.text: A key purpose of bank recapitalization is to __________.
options: strengthen banks' capital base so they can better absorb losses and support larger-scale lending
weaken the financial strength of banks
eliminate the central bank's regulatory role
reduce the number of customers a bank can serve
Economic Systems.correct_answer: strengthen banks' capital base so they can better absorb losses and support larger-scale lending

Economic Systems.text: Following the 2005 banking consolidation exercise in Nigeria, the number of licensed banks fell from about 89 to approximately __________.
The main difference between privatization and commercialization is that __________.
options: commercialization always transfers full ownership to private individuals
there is no real difference between the two terms
privatization only applies to agricultural enterprises
privatization transfers ownership to private hands, while commercialization makes a state enterprise operate on a profit-oriented, self-sustaining basis while remaining government-owned
Economic Systems.correct_answer: privatization transfers ownership to private hands, while commercialization makes a state enterprise operate on a profit-oriented, self-sustaining basis while remaining government-owned

Economic Systems.text: Commercialization of a public enterprise means __________.
options: transferring the enterprise entirely to foreign investors
converting the enterprise into a cooperative society
running the enterprise to operate profitably like a private business, while ownership may remain with government
Economic Systems.correct_answer: running the enterprise to operate profitably like a private business, while ownership may remain with government

Economic Systems.text: Nigeria's economy is best classified as a mixed economy because __________.
options: it exhibits features of both private enterprise and government participation and regulation
it operates strictly on barter trade
the government owns 100% of all businesses
there is no private sector activity at all
Economic Systems.correct_answer: it exhibits features of both private enterprise and government participation and regulation

Economic Systems.text: Public enterprises are business organizations that are __________.
options: owned and controlled wholly or mainly by government
prohibited from operating in any sector
owned by a single private individual
Economic Systems.correct_answer: owned and controlled wholly or mainly by government

Economic Systems.text: One benefit that has been associated with the privatization of public enterprises in Nigeria is __________.
options: guaranteed job security for all former public sector workers
complete removal of government from the economy
improved efficiency and service delivery due to profit-driven private management
Economic Systems.correct_answer: improved efficiency and service delivery due to profit-driven private management

Economic Systems.text: A common criticism (demerit) of privatization is that it may lead to __________.
options: improved competition in every case with no drawbacks
job losses and, in some cases, the replacement of a state monopoly with a private monopoly
an automatic reduction in the price of goods produced
an increase in government ownership of enterprises
Economic Systems.correct_answer: job losses and, in some cases, the replacement of a state monopoly with a private monopoly

Economic Systems.text: The Structural Adjustment Programme (SAP) introduced in Nigeria in 1986 was mainly aimed at __________.
options: restructuring and diversifying the economy away from oil dependence through market-oriented reforms
increasing government control over all sectors of the economy
Economic Systems.correct_answer: restructuring and diversifying the economy away from oil dependence through market-oriented reforms

Economic Systems.text: Deregulation of the downstream petroleum sector in Nigeria has mainly involved __________.
options: allowing market forces, rather than government fiat, to determine the pump price of petroleum products
increasing government subsidies on petroleum products indefinitely
banning private companies from importing petroleum products
Economic Systems.correct_answer: allowing market forces, rather than government fiat, to determine the pump price of petroleum products

Economic Systems.text: A distinguishing organ found in a centrally planned (command) economy is the __________.
options: stock exchange operating freely without restriction
private board of a multinational corporation
central planning board or authority that sets production targets and quotas
independent trade unions that set all prices
Economic Systems.correct_answer: central planning board or authority that sets production targets and quotas

Economic Systems.text: In a capitalist economic system, competition among firms primarily serves to __________.
options: encourage efficiency, better quality goods, and lower prices for consumers
guarantee that only one firm survives in every industry
eliminate the need for consumers to make choices
Economic Systems.correct_answer: encourage efficiency, better quality goods, and lower prices for consumers

Economic Systems.text: The profit motive is generally regarded as the central driving force behind economic activity in __________.
Economic Systems.correct_answer: a capitalist (free enterprise) economy

Economic Systems.text: Resources tend to be allocated mainly through the free interaction of market demand and supply, with minimal government direction, under which economic system?
Economic Systems.correct_answer: Capitalist/free enterprise economy

Economic Systems.text: A key reason governments intervene in a mixed economy is to __________.
options: prevent any form of trade with other countries
correct market failures and promote social welfare while still allowing private enterprise to operate
Economic Systems.correct_answer: correct market failures and promote social welfare while still allowing private enterprise to operate

Economic Systems.text: The Bureau of Public Enterprises (BPE) in Nigeria is primarily responsible for __________.
options: setting interest rates for commercial banks
implementing and supervising the privatization and commercialization of public enterprises
Economic Systems.correct_answer: implementing and supervising the privatization and commercialization of public enterprises

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: The scientific approach in economics generally involves __________.
options: avoiding the use of any data or observation
the systematic formulation of hypotheses, collection of data, and testing of theories
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: the systematic formulation of hypotheses, collection of data, and testing of theories

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: The inductive method of economic analysis proceeds by __________.
options: generalizing from specific observations and facts to arrive at broad economic laws or theories
using only mathematical symbols without real data
starting from general principles and deriving specific conclusions
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: generalizing from specific observations and facts to arrive at broad economic laws or theories

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: The deductive method of economic analysis proceeds by __________.
options: starting from general assumptions or premises and logically reasoning to specific conclusions
collecting numerous specific facts before forming any general idea
avoiding the use of logic or assumptions
relying entirely on historical statistics without any theory
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: starting from general assumptions or premises and logically reasoning to specific conclusions

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: Which of the following best illustrates the inductive method in economics?
options: Using a mathematical model without reference to any real-world observation
Ignoring all data and stating a personal opinion
Observing the buying behaviour of many consumers over time and then formulating the general law of demand
Assuming the law of demand is true and predicting how a specific consumer will behave
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: Observing the buying behaviour of many consumers over time and then formulating the general law of demand

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: Which of the following best illustrates the deductive method in economics?
options: Interviewing traders without any theoretical framework
Collecting price and quantity data from many markets before forming a theory
Starting from the general assumption that consumers act rationally, and deducing how a particular consumer will respond to a price change
Recording historical rainfall data to predict crop yields
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: Starting from the general assumption that consumers act rationally, and deducing how a particular consumer will respond to a price change

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: Positive economics is concerned with __________.
options: recommendations on how the economy should be run
statements of what ought to be, based on value judgments
objective statements of fact that can be tested and verified against evidence
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: objective statements of fact that can be tested and verified against evidence

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: Normative economics is concerned with __________.
options: value judgments and statements of what ought to be, reflecting opinions about desirability
mathematical proofs without any policy relevance
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: value judgments and statements of what ought to be, reflecting opinions about desirability

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: Which of the following is an example of a positive economic statement?
options: The minimum wage ought to be increased for the sake of fairness
The government should reduce fuel subsidies immediately
It is unfair that the rich pay the same tax rate as the poor
A rise in the price of petrol led to a fall in the quantity of petrol demanded last year
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: A rise in the price of petrol led to a fall in the quantity of petrol demanded last year

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: Which of the following is an example of a normative economic statement?
options: Government should increase spending on education because it is the right thing to do
Unemployment increased by two percent between two years
Nigeria's inflation rate rose to 24 percent in a given year
The exchange rate depreciated against the dollar last quarter
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: Government should increase spending on education because it is the right thing to do

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: An economic model may be described as __________.
options: a simplified representation of economic reality, often using assumptions, to explain or predict economic behaviour
a government document listing tax rates
a complete and exact replica of the entire economy with no simplification
a physical toy used to teach children about money
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: a simplified representation of economic reality, often using assumptions, to explain or predict economic behaviour

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: The Latin expression "ceteris paribus," frequently used in economic analysis, means __________.
options: other things being equal or held constant
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: other things being equal or held constant

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: Economists make simplifying assumptions such as ceteris paribus mainly in order to __________.
options: eliminate the need for economic theory altogether
isolate the effect of one variable on another by holding all other influencing factors constant
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: isolate the effect of one variable on another by holding all other influencing factors constant

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: In economic analysis, a table is a useful tool mainly because it __________.
options: is less accurate than a paragraph of text
can only be used to display qualitative opinions
presents numerical data in an organized, easy-to-read row-and-column format for comparison
replaces the need for any numerical data
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: presents numerical data in an organized, easy-to-read row-and-column format for comparison

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: Graphs are used in economic analysis primarily to __________.
options: replace the need for economic theory
eliminate the need for units of measurement
visually illustrate the relationship between two or more economic variables
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: visually illustrate the relationship between two or more economic variables

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: A pie chart is a statistical tool that is best suited for showing __________.
options: the proportion of a whole that is made up of different components, usually as segments of a circle
the exact numerical value of every data point without approximation
the correlation between two continuous variables
changes in a variable continuously over time
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: the proportion of a whole that is made up of different components, usually as segments of a circle

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: A bar chart is a statistical tool typically used to __________.
options: show the composition of a single total as slices of a circle
compare the magnitude of different categories of data using bars of varying length or height
display only continuous time-series data with a single line
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: compare the magnitude of different categories of data using bars of varying length or height

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: A line graph is particularly useful in economics for showing __________.
options: the trend of a variable such as price or output over a period of time
unrelated categorical data with no order
the exact proportion of a whole represented by a single category
the mode of a set of data
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: the trend of a variable such as price or output over a period of time

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: On a standard two-variable economic graph, the independent variable is conventionally plotted on the __________.
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: horizontal (x) axis

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: On a standard two-variable economic graph, the dependent variable is conventionally plotted on the __________.
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: vertical (y) axis

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: A measure of central tendency is a single value that __________.
options: shows only the highest value in a data set
represents the typical or middle value around which a set of data tends to cluster
lists every individual value in a data set
shows the spread or variability of a set of data
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: represents the typical or middle value around which a set of data tends to cluster

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: The arithmetic mean of a set of numbers is calculated by __________.
options: arranging the numbers in order and picking the middle value
identifying the value that occurs most frequently
dividing the sum of all the values by the number of values
subtracting the smallest value from the largest value
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: dividing the sum of all the values by the number of values

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: What is the mean of the numbers 4, 6, 8, 10, and 12?
The median of a set of data is __________.
options: the difference between the highest and lowest values
the sum of all values divided by their number
the middle value when the data are arranged in order of size
the value that occurs most frequently
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: the middle value when the data are arranged in order of size

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: What is the median of the data set: 3, 7, 5, 9, 1?
What is the median of the data set: 2, 4, 6, 8?
The mode of a set of data refers to __________.
options: the range between the highest and lowest values
the value that appears most frequently in the data set
the middle value of the ordered data
the average of all the values
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: the value that appears most frequently in the data set

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: What is the mode of the data set: 2, 3, 3, 4, 5, 3, 6?
The mean is generally considered a less reliable measure of central tendency when a data set contains __________.
options: extreme values (outliers) that can distort the average
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: extreme values (outliers) that can distort the average

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: Dispersion, in statistics, refers to __________.
options: the most frequently occurring value in a data set
the extent to which individual data values are spread out or scattered around the central value
the total number of observations in a data set
the typical or average value of a data set
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: the extent to which individual data values are spread out or scattered around the central value

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: The range of a set of data is calculated as __________.
options: the difference between the highest and lowest values in the data set
the sum of all the values divided by their number
the middle value of the ordered data
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: the difference between the highest and lowest values in the data set

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: What is the range of the data set: 5, 12, 8, 20, 3?
Variance, as a measure of dispersion, is defined as __________.
options: the simple difference between the highest and lowest values
the most frequently occurring value in the data
the average of the squared deviations of each value from the mean
the middle value of an ordered data set
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: the average of the squared deviations of each value from the mean

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: The standard deviation of a data set is __________.
options: the square root of the variance
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: the square root of the variance

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: Given the data set 2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9 (mean = 5), the standard deviation is approximately __________.
A relatively low standard deviation for a set of economic data (e.g. monthly prices) indicates that __________.
options: the values are closely clustered around the mean, showing low variability
the data set has no mean at all
the values are widely spread out and highly variable
the mode and median must be equal to zero
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: the values are closely clustered around the mean, showing low variability

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: A relatively high standard deviation for a set of economic data indicates that __________.
options: the values are widely spread out from the mean, showing high variability
the data set contains only one observation
the values are tightly clustered around the mean
all the values in the data set are identical
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: the values are widely spread out from the mean, showing high variability

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: Of the three common measures of central tendency, the one most affected by extremely large or small values (outliers) is the __________.
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: mean

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: Which measure of central tendency is generally least affected by extreme values in a data set?
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: Median

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: The deductive method of economic reasoning is also sometimes referred to as the __________.
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: a priori (or abstract) method

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: The inductive method of economic reasoning is also sometimes referred to as the __________.
options: empirical or a posteriori method, based on observed facts
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: empirical or a posteriori method, based on observed facts

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: Statistics plays an important role in economics mainly because it helps economists to __________.
options: avoid the need for any data collection
eliminate the need for economic theory
collect, organize, analyze, and interpret numerical economic data to test theories and inform decisions
make economics a purely subjective discipline
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: collect, organize, analyze, and interpret numerical economic data to test theories and inform decisions

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: A frequency distribution is __________.
options: a graph showing only two data points
a single average value representing a data set
a tabular summary showing how often each value or range of values occurs in a data set
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: a tabular summary showing how often each value or range of values occurs in a data set

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: A histogram differs from a simple bar chart mainly in that a histogram __________.
options: cannot be used to represent numerical data at all
always has gaps between adjacent bars
is used to display continuous, grouped frequency data with bars drawn without gaps between them
can only be used for qualitative, non-numerical data
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: is used to display continuous, grouped frequency data with bars drawn without gaps between them

Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.text: A scatter diagram is most useful in economic analysis for __________.
options: calculating the mode of a data set directly
showing the proportion of a whole made up by different categories
revealing whether a relationship or correlation exists between two variables, such as income and consumption
Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis.correct_answer: revealing whether a relationship or correlation exists between two variables, such as income and consumption

The Theory of Demand.text: In economics, 'demand' for a commodity refers to which of the following?
options: The desire to own a commodity regardless of price
The amount of a commodity produced by firms
The total stock of a commodity available in the market
The quantity of a commodity a consumer is willing and able to buy at a given price
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: The quantity of a commodity a consumer is willing and able to buy at a given price

The Theory of Demand.text: Which of the following best distinguishes 'demand' from a mere 'desire' for a commodity?
options: Demand must be backed by the ability and willingness to pay
Desire is always greater than demand
Demand only applies to luxury goods
Desire requires money while demand does not
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: Demand must be backed by the ability and willingness to pay

The Theory of Demand.text: Which of the following is the most important determinant of the demand for a commodity?
options: The price of the commodity itself
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: The price of the commodity itself

The Theory of Demand.text: An increase in a consumer's income is most likely to lead to which of the following, other things being equal?
options: A decrease in demand for all goods
No change in demand for any good
A decrease in the price of the good
An increase in demand for normal goods
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: An increase in demand for normal goods

The Theory of Demand.text: A change in consumer taste and preference in favour of a commodity will cause which of the following?
options: A leftward shift of the demand curve
A rightward shift of the demand curve
A movement down the existing demand curve
No change in the demand curve
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: A rightward shift of the demand curve

The Theory of Demand.text: If the price of tea rises and, as a result, the demand for coffee rises, tea and coffee are best described as
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: Substitute goods

The Theory of Demand.text: An increase in population size is likely to have which effect on the market demand for basic foodstuffs?
options: It has no effect on demand
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: It increases demand

The Theory of Demand.text: If consumers expect the price of rice to rise sharply next month, what will most likely happen to the current demand for rice?
options: Rice will become a Giffen good
Current demand will rise as consumers buy more now
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: Current demand will rise as consumers buy more now

The Theory of Demand.text: A demand schedule is best defined as
options: A graph showing quantity supplied at various prices
A table showing the various quantities of a commodity that will be bought at different prices over a period
A list of consumers who buy a commodity
A record of a firm's total sales revenue
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: A table showing the various quantities of a commodity that will be bought at different prices over a period

The Theory of Demand.text: When a demand schedule is plotted on a graph with price on the vertical axis and quantity on the horizontal axis, the resulting curve is
options: Upward sloping from left to right
Downward sloping from left to right
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: Downward sloping from left to right

The Theory of Demand.text: The law of demand states that, other things being equal,
options: The higher the price of a commodity, the higher the quantity demanded
The lower the price of a commodity, the lower the quantity demanded
The lower the price of a commodity, the higher the quantity demanded
Price and quantity demanded are unrelated
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: The lower the price of a commodity, the higher the quantity demanded

The Theory of Demand.text: Which of the following best explains why demand curves generally slope downward?
options: Firms always reduce output when prices fall
As price falls, the substitution and income effects make consumers buy more
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: As price falls, the substitution and income effects make consumers buy more

The Theory of Demand.text: A Giffen good is an exception to the law of demand because
options: Its demand curve is perfectly elastic
More of it is bought as its price falls, contrary to normal expectation
It has no substitutes at all
Less of it is bought as its price falls, contrary to normal expectation
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: Less of it is bought as its price falls, contrary to normal expectation

The Theory of Demand.text: Goods bought mainly for prestige, such that demand rises as price rises, are known as
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: Veblen (ostentatious) goods

The Theory of Demand.text: A change in the quantity demanded of a good, caused solely by a change in its own price, is represented on a demand diagram by
options: A shift of the entire demand curve to the right
A shift of the entire demand curve to the left
A movement along the same demand curve
A rotation of the demand curve about the origin
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: A movement along the same demand curve

The Theory of Demand.text: A change in demand, as opposed to a change in quantity demanded, is caused by
options: A change in the price of the commodity itself only
A change in the units used to measure quantity
A movement along the demand curve
A change in a non-price determinant such as income or taste
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: A change in a non-price determinant such as income or taste

The Theory of Demand.text: An increase in demand is graphically represented by
options: A rightward shift of the demand curve
A leftward shift of the demand curve
A downward movement along the demand curve
An upward movement along the demand curve
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: A rightward shift of the demand curve

The Theory of Demand.text: A decrease in demand for a commodity, due to a fall in consumer income for a normal good, is shown by
options: A rightward shift of the demand curve
A leftward shift of the demand curve
A movement down the demand curve
No change in the curve at all
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: A leftward shift of the demand curve

The Theory of Demand.text: Composite demand refers to a situation in which
options: A commodity is demanded for two or more different uses
Two commodities are demanded together because they complement each other
A commodity has many competing substitutes
Demand for a factor arises from demand for the good it produces
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: A commodity is demanded for two or more different uses

The Theory of Demand.text: Which of the following is the best example of composite demand?
options: Demand for car and demand for petrol
Demand for milk used for drinking, making cheese, and making butter
Demand for tea as a substitute for coffee
Demand for cotton because of the demand for cloth
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: Demand for milk used for drinking, making cheese, and making butter

The Theory of Demand.text: The demand for bricklayers that arises because of the demand for houses is an example of
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: Derived demand

The Theory of Demand.text: Derived demand can best be described as
options: Demand for a good arising because it is needed to produce another good or service
Demand for two goods that are consumed together
Demand for a good that has close substitutes
Demand that fluctuates with the season
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: Demand for a good arising because it is needed to produce another good or service

The Theory of Demand.text: When two or more commodities such as tea and coffee satisfy the same want and compete for the consumer's preference, this is known as
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: Competitive demand

The Theory of Demand.text: Joint demand exists when
options: Two goods are used together to satisfy a single want, such as cars and petrol
A single good satisfies several different wants
Two goods substitute for each other
A good is demanded only during a particular season
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: Two goods are used together to satisfy a single want, such as cars and petrol

The Theory of Demand.text: Bread and butter are typically bought together; economists describe such goods as being in
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: Joint demand

The Theory of Demand.text: Price elasticity of demand measures
options: The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in the price of the commodity
The responsiveness of supply to a change in price
The change in total revenue over time
The responsiveness of income to a change in price
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in the price of the commodity

The Theory of Demand.text: Demand for a commodity is said to be elastic when
options: The percentage change in quantity demanded is less than the percentage change in price
The percentage change in quantity demanded equals the percentage change in price
The percentage change in quantity demanded is greater than the percentage change in price
Quantity demanded does not respond at all to price changes
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: The percentage change in quantity demanded is greater than the percentage change in price

The Theory of Demand.text: Demand for a commodity is said to be inelastic when
options: The percentage change in quantity demanded is less than the percentage change in price
The percentage change in quantity demanded is greater than the percentage change in price
A small change in price causes an infinitely large change in quantity demanded
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: The percentage change in quantity demanded is less than the percentage change in price

The Theory of Demand.text: When the percentage change in quantity demanded exactly equals the percentage change in price, demand is said to be
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: Unitary elastic

The Theory of Demand.text: A demand curve that is a vertical straight line represents demand that is
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: Perfectly inelastic

The Theory of Demand.text: A demand curve that is a horizontal straight line represents demand that is
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: Perfectly elastic

The Theory of Demand.text: The price of a commodity rises from ₦10 to ₦12 and, as a result, quantity demanded falls from 100 units to 90 units. Using the percentage method, the price elasticity of demand (ignoring sign) is approximately
The price of a good falls from ₦20 to ₦16 (a 20% fall), causing quantity demanded to rise from 50 units to 70 units (a 40% rise). The price elasticity of demand (ignoring sign) is
If the price of a good increases by 10% and quantity demanded falls by exactly 10%, the coefficient of price elasticity of demand is
Income elasticity of demand measures
options: The responsiveness of demand for a good to a change in the price of another good
The responsiveness of demand for a good to a change in consumer income
The responsiveness of supply to a change in income
The responsiveness of price to a change in demand
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: The responsiveness of demand for a good to a change in consumer income

The Theory of Demand.text: A good whose demand rises as consumer income rises is called a
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: Normal good

The Theory of Demand.text: A good whose demand falls as consumer income rises, such as demand for garri among richer households, is called a(n)
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: Inferior good

The Theory of Demand.text: A luxury good typically has an income elasticity of demand that is
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: Greater than 1

The Theory of Demand.text: A basic necessity such as salt usually has an income elasticity of demand that is
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: Positive but less than 1

The Theory of Demand.text: Cross elasticity of demand measures
options: The responsiveness of quantity demanded of one good to a change in the price of another good
The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in its own price
The responsiveness of demand to a change in income
The responsiveness of supply to a change in price
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: The responsiveness of quantity demanded of one good to a change in the price of another good

The Theory of Demand.text: If a rise in the price of Good X causes the demand for Good Y to rise, the cross elasticity of demand between X and Y is
options: Positive, indicating X and Y are substitutes
Negative, indicating X and Y are substitutes
Positive, indicating X and Y are complements
Negative, indicating X and Y are complements
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: Positive, indicating X and Y are substitutes

The Theory of Demand.text: If a rise in the price of Good X causes the demand for Good Y to fall, X and Y are said to be
options: Unrelated goods with zero cross elasticity
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: Complements with negative cross elasticity

The Theory of Demand.text: Which of the following is NOT a major factor influencing the price elasticity of demand for a commodity?
options: The proportion of income spent on the commodity
The colour of the packaging used by the manufacturer
The time period allowed for consumers to adjust
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: The colour of the packaging used by the manufacturer

The Theory of Demand.text: Knowledge of price elasticity of demand is most useful to a firm or government when
options: Deciding the colour scheme of a product's logo
Setting prices and taxes to predict the effect on revenue and consumption
Determining the exact date a factory was built
Choosing the firm's registered office address
The Theory of Demand.correct_answer: Setting prices and taxes to predict the effect on revenue and consumption

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: Utility, in economics, is best defined as
options: The market price of a commodity
The quantity of a commodity supplied
The cost of producing a commodity
The satisfaction a consumer derives from consuming a commodity
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: The satisfaction a consumer derives from consuming a commodity

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: The cardinal utility approach to consumer behaviour assumes that
options: Utility cannot be measured at all
Utility is the same for every consumer
Consumers can only rank preferences without measuring them
Utility can be measured numerically, for example in 'utils'
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: Utility can be measured numerically, for example in 'utils'

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: The ordinal utility approach differs from the cardinal approach in that it assumes
options: Utility can be measured precisely in numbers
Consumers can only rank bundles of goods in order of preference, not measure satisfaction numerically
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: Consumers can only rank bundles of goods in order of preference, not measure satisfaction numerically

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: Total utility refers to
options: The satisfaction derived from consuming one additional unit of a good
The average satisfaction per unit consumed
The overall satisfaction a consumer derives from consuming a given quantity of a good
The satisfaction lost from consuming too much of a good
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: The overall satisfaction a consumer derives from consuming a given quantity of a good

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: Marginal utility is best defined as
options: Total utility divided by the number of units consumed
The total satisfaction from all goods consumed
The satisfaction derived from the very first unit consumed only
The additional satisfaction obtained from consuming one more unit of a good
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: The additional satisfaction obtained from consuming one more unit of a good

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: Average utility is calculated as
options: Marginal utility multiplied by total units
The highest utility obtained from any single unit
The change in total utility divided by the change in price
Total utility divided by the number of units consumed
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: Total utility divided by the number of units consumed

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: The law of diminishing marginal utility states that
options: As more units of a good are consumed, total utility falls continuously
Average utility always exceeds marginal utility
Marginal utility increases as more units are consumed
As more units of a good are consumed, the marginal utility from each additional unit eventually decreases
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: As more units of a good are consumed, the marginal utility from each additional unit eventually decreases

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: A consumer's total utility from bread reaches its maximum when
options: Marginal utility is at its highest
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: Marginal utility is zero

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: If marginal utility becomes negative after a certain level of consumption, this means that
options: Total utility begins to fall as more units are consumed
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: Total utility begins to fall as more units are consumed

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: The table below shows a consumer's utility from consuming units of oranges: 1st unit = 20 utils (total), 2nd unit total = 36 utils, 3rd unit total = 46 utils. The marginal utility of the 3rd unit is
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: 10 utils

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: Using the table: 1st unit total utility = 20, 2nd unit total utility = 36, the marginal utility of the 2nd unit is
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: 16 utils

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: The law of diminishing marginal utility helps to explain why
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: Demand curves generally slope downward

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: An indifference curve represents
options: Combinations of two goods that cost the same amount
The maximum output a firm can produce with given resources
The set of prices a firm is willing to charge
Combinations of two goods that yield the same total utility to a consumer
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: Combinations of two goods that yield the same total utility to a consumer

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: A key property of indifference curves is that they
options: Slope upward from left to right
Are usually convex to the origin and slope downward from left to right
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: Are usually convex to the origin and slope downward from left to right

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: Two indifference curves belonging to the same consumer can never intersect because
options: Intersection would imply inconsistent preference rankings
Curves are always parallel by definition
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: Intersection would imply inconsistent preference rankings

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: A higher indifference curve, further from the origin, represents
options: The same level of satisfaction as a lower curve
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: A higher level of satisfaction

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: The budget line (or price line) shows
options: All combinations of two goods a consumer can buy with a fixed income at given prices
All combinations of two goods that give equal satisfaction
The firm's total cost of production
The government's total budget for the year
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: All combinations of two goods a consumer can buy with a fixed income at given prices

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: If a consumer's income rises while prices remain constant, the budget line will
options: Shift outward, parallel to the original line
Shift inward, parallel to the original line
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: Shift outward, parallel to the original line

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: If the price of the good on the horizontal axis rises while income and the other good's price stay constant, the budget line will
options: Pivot outward on the vertical axis
Pivot inward on the horizontal axis, becoming steeper
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: Pivot inward on the horizontal axis, becoming steeper

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: Under the indifference curve approach, consumer equilibrium is reached at the point where
options: The budget line crosses the horizontal axis
The budget line is tangent to the highest attainable indifference curve
The indifference curve intersects the vertical axis
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: The budget line is tangent to the highest attainable indifference curve

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: At the point of consumer equilibrium on an indifference curve diagram, the slope of the indifference curve (marginal rate of substitution) equals
options: The slope of the budget line (the price ratio of the two goods)
The marginal utility of money only
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: The slope of the budget line (the price ratio of the two goods)

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: Under the marginal utility (cardinal) approach, a rational consumer allocating a fixed income between two goods X and Y is in equilibrium when
options: MUx equals MUy regardless of price
Total utility from X equals total utility from Y
The prices of X and Y are equal
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: MUx / Px equals MUy / Py

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: This equilibrium condition, MUx/Px = MUy/Py = ... , is known as the
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: Law of equi-marginal utility

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: If MUx/Px is greater than MUy/Py for a consumer, a rational consumer should
options: Buy more of Y and less of X
Buy more of X and less of Y
Buy equal amounts of X and Y regardless
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: Buy more of X and less of Y

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: Suppose the marginal utility of the last unit of good X consumed is 40 utils and its price is ₦20, while the marginal utility of the last unit of good Y is 30 utils and its price is ₦10. To reach equilibrium, the consumer should
options: Buy more of X since MUx/Px (2) is less than MUy/Py (3)
Buy more of Y since MUy/Py (3) is greater than MUx/Px (2)
Buy less of Y since it gives less utility per naira
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: Buy more of Y since MUy/Py (3) is greater than MUx/Px (2)

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: Consumer surplus is best defined as
options: The difference between what a consumer is willing to pay for a good and what they actually pay
The profit a firm makes on selling a good
The tax paid on a good by the consumer
The total amount spent on all goods by a consumer
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: The difference between what a consumer is willing to pay for a good and what they actually pay

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: On a normal downward-sloping demand curve diagram, consumer surplus is represented by the area
options: Below the price line and above the demand curve, up to the quantity bought
Above the price line and below the demand curve, up to the quantity bought
To the right of the demand curve only
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: Above the price line and below the demand curve, up to the quantity bought

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: A consumer is willing to pay ₦500 for a bag of rice but the market price is ₦350. The consumer surplus on this purchase is
Other things being equal, a fall in the market price of a good will cause consumer surplus to
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: Rise

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: The 'water-diamond paradox' in consumer theory refers to the observation that
options: Water, though essential, is cheap, while diamonds, though non-essential, are expensive, explained by marginal rather than total utility
Diamonds are more useful than water in everyday life
Water has no utility to consumers
Prices are always equal to total utility
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: Water, though essential, is cheap, while diamonds, though non-essential, are expensive, explained by marginal rather than total utility

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: Which basic assumption is typically made about a rational consumer in utility theory?
options: The consumer aims to maximise total utility subject to their income constraint
The consumer aims to minimise total utility
The consumer ignores prices when choosing goods
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: The consumer aims to maximise total utility subject to their income constraint

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: If total utility from consuming 4 oranges is 60 utils, the average utility per orange is
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: 15 utils

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: A consumer continues to buy successive units of a good only up to the point where marginal utility per unit of money spent equals
options: The market price of the good
The marginal utility of money (or of the last unit of money spent elsewhere)
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: The marginal utility of money (or of the last unit of money spent elsewhere)

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: Which of the following is a criticism of the cardinal (marginal utility) approach to consumer behaviour?
options: It correctly assumes utility can be measured exactly like weight or length
It is unrealistic to assume that satisfaction can be measured numerically in utils
It does not use the concept of price at all
It has no relationship with the law of demand
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: It is unrealistic to assume that satisfaction can be measured numerically in utils

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: The marginal rate of substitution (MRS) between two goods measures
options: The rate at which a consumer is willing to give up one good for an extra unit of another good while remaining equally satisfied
The rate at which the price of one good changes relative to another
The total income spent on both goods
The ratio of total utility to marginal utility
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: The rate at which a consumer is willing to give up one good for an extra unit of another good while remaining equally satisfied

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: As a consumer moves down along a typical convex indifference curve, the marginal rate of substitution
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: Diminishes

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: An area on a graph that lies below the budget line and below the highest attainable indifference curve, but is not the point of tangency, represents a combination of goods that is
options: Attainable but gives less than maximum satisfaction
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: Attainable but gives less than maximum satisfaction

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: A point lying beyond (outside) the consumer's budget line represents a combination of goods that is
options: Unattainable given the consumer's current income and prices
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: Unattainable given the consumer's current income and prices

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: Which of the following statements about total utility and marginal utility is correct?
options: Total utility rises as long as marginal utility is positive
Total utility falls whenever marginal utility is positive
Marginal utility and total utility always move in the same direction at the same rate
Total utility is unrelated to marginal utility
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: Total utility rises as long as marginal utility is positive

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: Suppose a consumer eats plates of rice: MU of 1st plate = 30 utils, MU of 2nd plate = 20 utils, MU of 3rd plate = 8 utils. The total utility after eating 3 plates is
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: 58 utils

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: The behaviour of marginal utilities in question 40 (30, 20, then 8) illustrates
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: Diminishing marginal utility

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: Which of the following goods would most likely show diminishing marginal utility very quickly to an average consumer within a single sitting?
options: Successive glasses of water when already very thirsty and then full
The first unit of currency earned
Land, which cannot be consumed directly
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: Successive glasses of water when already very thirsty and then full

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: In indifference curve analysis, the assumption that a consumer prefers more of a good to less is known as the assumption of
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: Non-satiation (more is preferred to less)

The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.text: Compared to the cardinal utility approach, the indifference curve (ordinal) approach is generally considered more realistic because it
options: Requires consumers only to rank preferences rather than assign exact numerical values to satisfaction
Assumes money has constant marginal utility
Requires more precise numerical data than the cardinal approach
The Theory of Consumer Behaviour.correct_answer: Requires consumers only to rank preferences rather than assign exact numerical values to satisfaction

The Theory of Supply.text: In economics, 'supply' of a commodity refers to
options: The total quantity of a commodity in existence
The amount of a commodity a consumer wishes to buy
The quantity of a commodity that producers are willing and able to offer for sale at a given price over a period
The stock of raw materials held by a firm
The Theory of Supply.correct_answer: The quantity of a commodity that producers are willing and able to offer for sale at a given price over a period

The Theory of Supply.text: Which of the following is generally the most important determinant of the supply of a commodity?
options: The price of the commodity itself
The Theory of Supply.correct_answer: The price of the commodity itself

The Theory of Supply.text: A rise in the cost of raw materials used to produce a commodity will most likely cause
options: An increase in supply at every price
