National Income.text: Real GDP differs from nominal GDP in that real GDP is...
options: adjusted for price changes (inflation), while nominal GDP is measured in current prices
National Income.correct_answer: adjusted for price changes (inflation), while nominal GDP is measured in current prices

National Income.text: Per capita income is calculated by...
options: dividing national income by the number of workers only
dividing national income by total population
National Income.correct_answer: dividing national income by total population

National Income.text: Which of the following best illustrates the "problem of double counting" in national income measurement?
options: including wages paid to workers once
including the value of a single final good once
excluding transfer payments from national income
including both the value of flour sold to a bakery and the value of the bread made from that flour, without netting out the flour cost
National Income.correct_answer: including both the value of flour sold to a bakery and the value of the bread made from that flour, without netting out the flour cost

National Income.text: Depreciation, in national income accounting, refers to...
options: the wearing out or using up of capital equipment (capital consumption) over the year
a fall in the value of a country's currency
National Income.correct_answer: the wearing out or using up of capital equipment (capital consumption) over the year

National Income.text: Which sector's output is notoriously difficult to value accurately in national income accounts of developing countries?
National Income.correct_answer: the informal/subsistence sector

National Income.text: National income at factor cost is obtained from national income at market prices by...
options: adding indirect taxes and deducting subsidies
deducting indirect taxes and adding subsidies
National Income.correct_answer: deducting indirect taxes and adding subsidies

National Income.text: Which of the following is an injection, rather than a leakage, in the circular flow of income?
National Income.correct_answer: government spending

National Income.text: A rise in national income is likely to lead to a rise in imports because of...
National Income.correct_answer: the marginal propensity to import

National Income.text: Which of the following best describes "net investment"?
National Income.correct_answer: gross investment minus depreciation

National Income.text: The main purpose of using the "final goods" concept in GDP calculation is to...
options: increase the measured value of GDP artificially
avoid double counting of intermediate goods
National Income.correct_answer: avoid double counting of intermediate goods

National Income.text: National income accounting problems in Nigeria include all of the following EXCEPT...
options: excessive computerization of records leading to inflated figures
National Income.correct_answer: excessive computerization of records leading to inflated figures

National Income.text: If a country's GNP is ₦500 billion and depreciation is ₦50 billion, its NNP is...
National Income.correct_answer: ₦450 billion

National Income.text: Which of the following best describes a limitation of the income approach regarding illegal or unreported income?
options: illegal incomes are always fully reported and included
illegal income increases GDP more than legal income does
incomes from illegal or unreported (black market) activities are typically excluded, understating national income
illegal income has no effect on national income statistics
National Income.correct_answer: incomes from illegal or unreported (black market) activities are typically excluded, understating national income

Money and Inflation.text: Money is best defined as...
options: anything generally acceptable as a medium of exchange for goods, services, and debts
only coins and notes issued by the central bank
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: anything generally acceptable as a medium of exchange for goods, services, and debts

Money and Inflation.text: Which of the following is NOT a function of money?
options: acting as a medium of exchange
acting as a store of value
acting as a unit of account
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: producing goods and services

Money and Inflation.text: The characteristic of money that allows it to be divided into smaller units without loss of value is...
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: divisibility

Money and Inflation.text: Which characteristic of money ensures it does not deteriorate quickly and can be used repeatedly?
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: durability

Money and Inflation.text: Money functioning as a "unit of account" means it is used to...
options: measure and express the value of goods and services
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: measure and express the value of goods and services

Money and Inflation.text: Trade by barter is difficult mainly because of...
options: the lack of double coincidence of wants
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: the lack of double coincidence of wants

Money and Inflation.text: The demand for money held for day-to-day transactions is called...
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: transactions demand for money

Money and Inflation.text: The demand for money held to meet unforeseen expenses is called...
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: precautionary demand for money

Money and Inflation.text: The speculative demand for money arises from the desire to...
options: hold money to take advantage of expected future changes in interest rates or asset prices
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: hold money to take advantage of expected future changes in interest rates or asset prices

Money and Inflation.text: The total supply of money in an economy typically includes...
options: currency in circulation plus demand deposits with banks
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: currency in circulation plus demand deposits with banks

Money and Inflation.text: According to the Quantity Theory of Money, the equation of exchange (Fisher's equation) is expressed as...
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: MV = PT

Money and Inflation.text: In the Fisher equation MV = PT, "V" represents...
options: the velocity of circulation of money
the volume of money in bank vaults
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: the velocity of circulation of money

Money and Inflation.text: According to the Quantity Theory of Money, if the money supply doubles while V and T remain constant, the price level will...
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: double

Money and Inflation.text: If M = ₦200 million, V = 5, and T = 1,000,000 transactions, then using MV = PT, the average price level P is approximately...
A rise in the general price level while the value of money falls illustrates that the value of money and the price level are...
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: inversely related

Money and Inflation.text: Inflation is best defined as...
options: a one-time rise in the price of a single good
a persistent (sustained) rise in the general price level over time
a fall in the general price level
a rise in the exchange rate only
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: a persistent (sustained) rise in the general price level over time

Money and Inflation.text: Demand-pull inflation occurs when...
options: production costs rise, pushing prices up
aggregate demand exceeds aggregate supply at full employment, pulling prices up
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: aggregate demand exceeds aggregate supply at full employment, pulling prices up

Money and Inflation.text: Cost-push inflation is primarily caused by...
options: a rise in production costs (e.g., wages, raw materials), which is passed on to consumers as higher prices
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: a rise in production costs (e.g., wages, raw materials), which is passed on to consumers as higher prices

Money and Inflation.text: Which of the following is a common cause of inflation in Nigeria?
options: excessive deficit financing and expansion of the money supply by government
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: excessive deficit financing and expansion of the money supply by government

Money and Inflation.text: The Consumer Price Index (CPI) is used to measure...
options: changes in the general price level of a basket of goods and services over time
the exchange rate of the naira
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: changes in the general price level of a basket of goods and services over time

Money and Inflation.text: Creeping inflation refers to...
options: a sudden and very rapid rise in prices
a slow and gradual rise in prices over time
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: a slow and gradual rise in prices over time

Money and Inflation.text: Hyperinflation refers to...
options: an extremely rapid and out-of-control rise in prices
a very slow rise in prices
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: an extremely rapid and out-of-control rise in prices

Money and Inflation.text: One negative effect of inflation on an economy is that it...
options: erodes the purchasing power of money and hurts fixed-income earners
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: erodes the purchasing power of money and hurts fixed-income earners

Money and Inflation.text: Which group tends to benefit from unanticipated inflation?
options: creditors, who are repaid with money that is worth less
debtors, who repay loans with money that is worth less
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: debtors, who repay loans with money that is worth less

Money and Inflation.text: A common monetary policy measure to control inflation is...
options: lowering interest rates to increase borrowing
raising interest rates to reduce money supply and borrowing
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: raising interest rates to reduce money supply and borrowing

Money and Inflation.text: A common fiscal policy measure to control demand-pull inflation is...
options: reducing government spending and/or increasing taxation
increasing government spending and reducing taxation
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: reducing government spending and/or increasing taxation

Money and Inflation.text: Deflation is best defined as...
options: a persistent rise in the general price level
a fall in exchange rates only
a persistent fall in the general price level
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: a persistent fall in the general price level

Money and Inflation.text: Deflation is typically measured using...
options: a rise in the exchange rate
a fall in the consumer price index (CPI) over time
an increase in the money supply
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: a fall in the consumer price index (CPI) over time

Money and Inflation.text: One major effect of deflation on an economy is...
options: rising business profits and full employment
falling business profits and rising unemployment as firms cut back production
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: falling business profits and rising unemployment as firms cut back production

Money and Inflation.text: A policy measure to control deflation is...
options: increasing government spending and/or lowering interest rates to stimulate demand
reducing government spending and raising interest rates
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: increasing government spending and/or lowering interest rates to stimulate demand

Money and Inflation.text: Legal tender money is money that...
options: can be refused by anyone at will
is only used for foreign trade
must be accepted by law in settlement of debt
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: must be accepted by law in settlement of debt

Money and Inflation.text: Token money refers to money whose...
options: face value equals its intrinsic value exactly
face value is greater than its intrinsic (metal/material) value
face value is less than its intrinsic value
value is determined only by the weight of metal it contains
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: face value is greater than its intrinsic (metal/material) value

Money and Inflation.text: Fiat money derives its value mainly from...
options: the gold it is backed by
government decree/order and general public acceptance, rather than from any intrinsic worth
its use as a raw material
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: government decree/order and general public acceptance, rather than from any intrinsic worth

Money and Inflation.text: Which of the following best illustrates the "store of value" function of money?
options: keeping savings in cash or a bank account for future use
using money to buy groceries today
using money to price goods in a shop
using money to pay wages this week
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: keeping savings in cash or a bank account for future use

Money and Inflation.text: An increase in the supply of money without a corresponding increase in output is likely to lead to...
options: a fall in interest rates only
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: inflation

Money and Inflation.text: Which of the following best describes "imported inflation"?
options: inflation caused by excess domestic demand
inflation caused by a rise in the prices of imported goods and raw materials
inflation caused by a fall in wages
inflation caused by falling import prices
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: inflation caused by a rise in the prices of imported goods and raw materials

Money and Inflation.text: The main way a central bank controls money supply to fight inflation is through...
options: fixing the prices of all goods directly
monetary policy tools such as open market operations and changes in the discount/interest rate
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: monetary policy tools such as open market operations and changes in the discount/interest rate

Money and Inflation.text: Which of the following is TRUE about the relationship between the value of money and inflation?
options: as inflation rises, the value (purchasing power) of money falls
as inflation rises, the value of money also rises
inflation has no effect on the value of money
the value of money always rises with the money supply
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: as inflation rises, the value (purchasing power) of money falls

Money and Inflation.text: One control measure for cost-push inflation is...
options: wage and price controls or restraint to limit cost increases
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: wage and price controls or restraint to limit cost increases

Money and Inflation.text: Under the Quantity Theory of Money, "T" in MV = PT represents...
options: the total volume/number of transactions in the economy
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: the total volume/number of transactions in the economy

Money and Inflation.text: Which of the following is an effect of deflation on debtors?
options: debtors benefit because money loses value
debtors are completely unaffected by deflation
debtors are worse off because they repay loans with money that is now worth more
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: debtors are worse off because they repay loans with money that is now worth more

Money and Inflation.text: A rise in the exchange value of a country's currency relative to others, alongside falling domestic prices, is most associated with...
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: deflation

Money and Inflation.text: Which of the following best defines "narrow money" (M1)?
options: currency plus all long-term savings and time deposits
the total value of government bonds
currency in circulation plus demand (current account) deposits
Money and Inflation.correct_answer: currency in circulation plus demand (current account) deposits

Financial Institutions.text: Which of the following is NOT a function of commercial banks?
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: Issuing legal tender currency

Financial Institutions.text: The main document a commercial bank customer uses to withdraw cash from a current account is the ____.
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: Cheque

Financial Institutions.text: Which type of bank account normally does NOT earn interest but allows withdrawal by cheque?
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: Current account

Financial Institutions.text: A bank overdraft is best described as ____.
options: a loan secured against landed property
an account that pays a fixed rate of interest over a fixed period
a facility for converting foreign currency to naira
permission for a customer to withdraw more than the balance in his account up to an agreed limit
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: permission for a customer to withdraw more than the balance in his account up to an agreed limit

Financial Institutions.text: The apex bank in Nigeria responsible for issuing the national currency is the ____.
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: Central Bank of Nigeria

Financial Institutions.text: Which of the following best describes the Central Bank of Nigeria's role as "lender of last resort"?
options: It lends only to the federal government
It provides emergency loans to commercial banks facing liquidity problems when no other source is available
It grants agricultural loans directly to farmers
It lends directly to individual members of the public
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: It provides emergency loans to commercial banks facing liquidity problems when no other source is available

Financial Institutions.text: Which of these is NOT a traditional function of the Central Bank of Nigeria?
options: Custodian of the country's foreign exchange reserves
Accepting deposits from ordinary members of the public for daily transactions
Regulation and supervision of the banking system
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: Accepting deposits from ordinary members of the public for daily transactions

Financial Institutions.text: A mortgage bank is primarily set up to ____.
options: provide short-term trade finance for importers
insure lives and properties against risk
deal exclusively in government treasury bills
finance the purchase and construction of residential and commercial buildings
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: finance the purchase and construction of residential and commercial buildings

Financial Institutions.text: Merchant banks differ from commercial banks mainly in that merchant banks ____.
options: focus on wholesale banking, corporate finance and long-term project funding
accept small savings deposits from individuals
are owned solely by the government
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: focus on wholesale banking, corporate finance and long-term project funding

Financial Institutions.text: Which of the following is a major function of insurance companies in an economy?
options: Spreading and pooling risk among policyholders in exchange for premiums
Granting mortgage loans for building houses
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: Spreading and pooling risk among policyholders in exchange for premiums

Financial Institutions.text: In insurance, the regular payment made by the insured to the insurer for cover against risk is called ____.
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: premium

Financial Institutions.text: A building society mainly specialises in ____.
options: underwriting new share issues for companies
buying and selling foreign currency for travellers
printing and distributing the national currency
mobilising savings and granting long-term loans for house purchase
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: mobilising savings and granting long-term loans for house purchase

Financial Institutions.text: Financial institutions promote economic development chiefly by ____.
options: mobilising savings and channelling them into productive investment
fixing the prices of all goods and services
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: mobilising savings and channelling them into productive investment

Financial Institutions.text: One way financial institutions contribute to economic development in Nigeria is by ____.
options: collecting import duties on behalf of government
providing credit facilities to entrepreneurs to expand production
fixing the exchange rate of the naira permanently
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: providing credit facilities to entrepreneurs to expand production

Financial Institutions.text: The market where short-term funds, with maturity of one year or less, are borrowed and lent is called the ____.
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: money market

Financial Institutions.text: The market that deals in long-term funds through instruments such as shares and debentures is the ____.
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: capital market

Financial Institutions.text: Which of the following is a money market instrument?
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: Treasury bills

Financial Institutions.text: Which of the following is traded in the capital market rather than the money market?
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: Ordinary shares

Financial Institutions.text: The Nigerian Stock Exchange is an example of an institution operating in the ____.
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: capital market

Financial Institutions.text: In Nigeria, the regulatory body responsible for supervising the capital market is the ____.
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: Securities and Exchange Commission

Financial Institutions.text: The body that insures deposits in Nigerian banks to protect depositors in case of bank failure is the ____.
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: Nigerian Deposit Insurance Corporation

Financial Institutions.text: The main instrument used by the Central Bank to regulate the money supply by buying and selling government securities is called ____.
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: open market operations

Financial Institutions.text: The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) refers to ____.
options: the interest rate charged on interbank loans
the maximum amount a bank can lend to one customer
the minimum proportion of total deposits banks must keep with the Central Bank
the exchange rate between the naira and the US dollar
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: the minimum proportion of total deposits banks must keep with the Central Bank

Financial Institutions.text: If the Central Bank wants to reduce the amount of credit banks can create, it should ____ the cash reserve ratio.
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: increase

Financial Institutions.text: The rate at which the Central Bank of Nigeria lends to commercial banks, serving as a benchmark for other interest rates, is officially called the ____.
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: Monetary Policy Rate

Financial Institutions.text: The Liquidity Ratio requires banks to hold a certain percentage of their deposits in ____.
options: readily convertible liquid assets such as cash and short-term securities
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: readily convertible liquid assets such as cash and short-term securities

Financial Institutions.text: When the Central Bank directs banks to lend more to preferred sectors like agriculture and less to others, it is applying ____.
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: selective credit control

Financial Institutions.text: "Moral suasion" as a tool of monetary policy refers to ____.
options: a law compelling banks to lend to government only
the printing of additional currency notes
the Central Bank using persuasion and appeals rather than force to influence bank behaviour
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: the Central Bank using persuasion and appeals rather than force to influence bank behaviour

Financial Institutions.text: Deposit money banks create credit mainly through the process of ____.
options: repeated lending and re-depositing of a fraction of deposits, expanding total deposits
collecting taxes on behalf of government
buying foreign exchange from the Central Bank
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: repeated lending and re-depositing of a fraction of deposits, expanding total deposits

Financial Institutions.text: If the required cash reserve ratio is 20%, the maximum credit (deposit) multiplier is ____.
A bank receives an initial deposit of ₦1,000,000 and the cash reserve ratio is 25%. The maximum additional amount the banking system can create in loans is ____.
Which of the following is a major challenge facing the Nigerian financial sector?
options: Excess liquidity with no lending opportunities
High rate of non-performing loans and loan defaults
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: High rate of non-performing loans and loan defaults

Financial Institutions.text: A key challenge limiting rural dwellers' access to formal banking services in Nigeria is ____.
options: low financial literacy and inadequate banking infrastructure in rural areas
too many bank branches in rural areas
excessive government subsidies to rural banks
the abolition of all interest rates
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: low financial literacy and inadequate banking infrastructure in rural areas

Financial Institutions.text: Which of the following best describes "financial inclusion" as a policy goal in Nigeria's financial sector?
options: Restricting banking services to urban elites only
Ensuring individuals and businesses have access to useful and affordable financial products and services
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: Ensuring individuals and businesses have access to useful and affordable financial products and services

Financial Institutions.text: Microfinance banks in Nigeria are primarily established to ____.
options: provide financial services to low-income earners and small businesses excluded from conventional banking
issue treasury bills on behalf of government
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: provide financial services to low-income earners and small businesses excluded from conventional banking

Financial Institutions.text: One key difference between commercial banks and merchant banks is that commercial banks ____.
options: cannot accept deposits from the public
deal mainly with individual retail customers and small deposits
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: deal mainly with individual retail customers and small deposits

Financial Institutions.text: A "standing order" given by a bank customer instructs the bank to ____.
options: make fixed, regular payments to a third party on specified dates
refuse all withdrawals from the account
convert the account to a foreign currency account
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: make fixed, regular payments to a third party on specified dates

Financial Institutions.text: Which of the following institutions would MOST likely underwrite a company's new share issue?
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: A merchant/investment bank

Financial Institutions.text: The main source of income for a commercial bank is the difference between ____.
options: interest earned on loans and interest paid on deposits
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: interest earned on loans and interest paid on deposits

Financial Institutions.text: Which of the following is a function of the Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC)?
options: Setting the exchange rate of the naira
Issuing shares on the stock exchange
Protecting depositors by guaranteeing payment of deposits up to a set limit if a bank fails
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: Protecting depositors by guaranteeing payment of deposits up to a set limit if a bank fails

Financial Institutions.text: Development banks such as the Bank of Industry differ from commercial banks in that they ____.
options: focus on providing medium- to long-term finance for specific development projects
are prohibited from lending to any business
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: focus on providing medium- to long-term finance for specific development projects

Financial Institutions.text: A key indicator that a financial institution is well-regulated in Nigeria is that it operates under the supervision of ____.
options: any private individual of its choice
the Central Bank of Nigeria and other statutory regulatory bodies
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: the Central Bank of Nigeria and other statutory regulatory bodies

Financial Institutions.text: Which of the following best distinguishes life insurance from general insurance?
options: Life insurance is compulsory for all citizens while general insurance is optional
General insurance only covers government property
Life insurance covers risks to human life while general insurance covers property, motor and other non-life risks
Life insurance premiums are paid by the government
Financial Institutions.correct_answer: Life insurance covers risks to human life while general insurance covers property, motor and other non-life risks

Public Finance.text: Public finance is best defined as the study of ____.
options: how government raises revenue and spends it to achieve economic objectives
how private individuals manage their household budgets
how firms maximise profit in the short run
Public Finance.correct_answer: how government raises revenue and spends it to achieve economic objectives

Public Finance.text: Which of the following is a major objective of public finance?
options: Maximising the profit of private companies
Equitable distribution of income and wealth among citizens
Fixing wages in the private sector
Public Finance.correct_answer: Equitable distribution of income and wealth among citizens

Public Finance.text: Fiscal policy refers to the use of ____ to influence the economy.
Public Finance.correct_answer: government revenue and expenditure

Public Finance.text: Which of the following is an instrument of fiscal policy?
Public Finance.correct_answer: Taxation

Public Finance.text: An expansionary fiscal policy typically involves ____.
options: increasing government spending and/or reducing taxes to stimulate the economy
reducing government spending and raising taxes
selling more treasury bills to mop up liquidity
Public Finance.correct_answer: increasing government spending and/or reducing taxes to stimulate the economy

Public Finance.text: A contractionary fiscal policy is most appropriate when the economy is experiencing ____.
options: high inflation caused by excess aggregate demand
Public Finance.correct_answer: high inflation caused by excess aggregate demand

Public Finance.text: Which of the following is a major source of government revenue in Nigeria?
Public Finance.correct_answer: Taxation

Public Finance.text: Royalties as a source of government revenue are payments received from ____.
options: companies exploiting natural resources such as crude oil and minerals
Public Finance.correct_answer: companies exploiting natural resources such as crude oil and minerals

Public Finance.text: Rent as a source of government revenue refers to income received from ____.
options: government-owned land and property leased to individuals or organisations
Public Finance.correct_answer: government-owned land and property leased to individuals or organisations

Public Finance.text: Grants and aids received by government from foreign countries or international organisations are examples of ____.
Public Finance.correct_answer: external non-tax revenue

Public Finance.text: A tax is best defined as ____.
options: a voluntary contribution made by citizens to charity
a loan given by government to private businesses
a compulsory levy imposed by government on individuals and firms without a direct benefit in return
a fee paid for a specific service rendered
Public Finance.correct_answer: a compulsory levy imposed by government on individuals and firms without a direct benefit in return

Public Finance.text: According to Adam Smith's canons of taxation, a good tax system should be ____.
Public Finance.correct_answer: convenient, certain, economical and equitable

Public Finance.text: The principle of taxation which states that a tax should be easy and convenient for the taxpayer to pay is called the canon of ____.
Public Finance.correct_answer: convenience

Public Finance.text: A direct tax is one that ____.
options: is levied on goods and services and can be shifted to another person
is levied on income or wealth and paid directly by the person on whom it is imposed
is collected only from foreign companies
is paid only by government agencies
Public Finance.correct_answer: is levied on income or wealth and paid directly by the person on whom it is imposed

Public Finance.text: Which of the following is an example of a direct tax in Nigeria?
Public Finance.correct_answer: Personal income tax

Public Finance.text: Which of the following is an example of an indirect tax?
Public Finance.correct_answer: Value Added Tax

Public Finance.text: An indirect tax is one whose burden ____.
options: can be shifted from the person who pays it to another person
can never be shifted to another person
is borne solely by the government
is always paid by foreign investors
Public Finance.correct_answer: can be shifted from the person who pays it to another person

Public Finance.text: A progressive tax system is one in which ____.
options: the rate of tax decreases as income increases
the rate of tax increases as the taxpayer's income increases
everyone pays the same fixed amount of tax regardless of income
the rate of tax remains constant regardless of income
Public Finance.correct_answer: the rate of tax increases as the taxpayer's income increases

Public Finance.text: A regressive tax takes ____.
options: a higher proportion of the income of high-income earners than of low-income earners
the same absolute amount from every taxpayer
a higher proportion of the income of low-income earners than of high-income earners
no money at all from low-income earners
Public Finance.correct_answer: a higher proportion of the income of low-income earners than of high-income earners

Public Finance.text: A proportional tax is one in which ____.
options: the tax rate rises as income rises
the tax rate falls as income rises
only the wealthy pay any tax at all
the same percentage rate of tax is charged regardless of the level of income
Public Finance.correct_answer: the same percentage rate of tax is charged regardless of the level of income

Public Finance.text: Nigeria's Personal Income Tax, with rates rising as income rises, is an example of a ____ tax.
Public Finance.correct_answer: progressive

Public Finance.text: A poll tax (or community tax) is a tax that ____.
options: is charged only on imported goods
charges every adult the same fixed amount regardless of income
varies according to the value of property owned
is charged only on company profits
Public Finance.correct_answer: charges every adult the same fixed amount regardless of income

Public Finance.text: Tax incidence refers to ____.
options: the total amount of tax collected by government in a year
the rate at which a tax is charged
the final resting place of the burden of a tax after any shifting has occurred
the number of taxpayers registered in a country
Public Finance.correct_answer: the final resting place of the burden of a tax after any shifting has occurred

Public Finance.text: One likely effect of a heavy tax on cigarettes is that ____.
options: the price of cigarettes will definitely fall
government revenue from cigarettes will always fall to zero
demand for cigarettes will become perfectly inelastic
producers may pass on part of the tax burden to consumers through higher prices
Public Finance.correct_answer: producers may pass on part of the tax burden to consumers through higher prices

Public Finance.text: A major effect of taxation on the economy is that it can be used to ____.
options: discourage the consumption of harmful goods such as tobacco and alcohol
increase the consumption of harmful goods
eliminate the need for government expenditure
Public Finance.correct_answer: discourage the consumption of harmful goods such as tobacco and alcohol

Public Finance.text: Which of the following is a likely effect of increased government (public) expenditure on infrastructure?
options: It always causes deflation in the economy
It can stimulate economic activity and create employment opportunities
It automatically reduces the national debt
It has no effect on aggregate demand
Public Finance.correct_answer: It can stimulate economic activity and create employment opportunities

Public Finance.text: Recurrent expenditure by government refers to spending on ____.
options: long-term capital projects such as roads and bridges
day-to-day running costs such as salaries and maintenance
Public Finance.correct_answer: day-to-day running costs such as salaries and maintenance

Public Finance.text: Capital expenditure by government refers to spending on ____.
options: long-term investment projects such as roads, bridges and schools
Public Finance.correct_answer: long-term investment projects such as roads, bridges and schools

Public Finance.text: A balanced budget occurs when ____.
options: government's total revenue equals its total expenditure
government spends without collecting any revenue
Public Finance.correct_answer: government's total revenue equals its total expenditure

Public Finance.text: A deficit budget occurs when ____.
options: government's expected revenue exceeds its planned expenditure
government's planned expenditure exceeds its expected revenue
government's revenue equals its expenditure exactly
government abolishes all forms of expenditure
Public Finance.correct_answer: government's planned expenditure exceeds its expected revenue

Public Finance.text: A surplus budget occurs when ____.
options: government's planned expenditure exceeds its expected revenue
government revenue and expenditure are exactly equal
government's expected revenue exceeds its planned expenditure
government has no revenue at all
Public Finance.correct_answer: government's expected revenue exceeds its planned expenditure

Public Finance.text: A common way for government to finance a budget deficit is through ____.
options: borrowing from within the country or from abroad
Public Finance.correct_answer: borrowing from within the country or from abroad

Public Finance.text: Public debt owed to lenders within the country is known as ____.
Public Finance.correct_answer: internal (domestic) debt

Public Finance.text: Public debt owed to foreign governments, institutions or creditors is known as ____.
Public Finance.correct_answer: external debt

Public Finance.text: A major danger of excessive external public debt for a country like Nigeria is that ____.
options: it automatically increases the value of the naira
it eliminates the need for taxation completely
a large share of government revenue may be used for debt servicing, leaving less for development
Public Finance.correct_answer: a large share of government revenue may be used for debt servicing, leaving less for development

Public Finance.text: Treasury bills and development stocks issued by government are examples of instruments used to raise ____.
Public Finance.correct_answer: internal public debt

Public Finance.text: Revenue allocation in Nigeria refers to ____.
options: the sharing of nationally generated revenue among the federal, state and local governments
the collection of personal income tax by state governments only
the sharing of profits among private shareholders
the distribution of import licences to traders
Public Finance.correct_answer: the sharing of nationally generated revenue among the federal, state and local governments

Public Finance.text: In Nigeria's federal system, the body constitutionally responsible for recommending revenue allocation formulas is the ____.
options: Revenue Mobilisation, Allocation and Fiscal Commission
Public Finance.correct_answer: Revenue Mobilisation, Allocation and Fiscal Commission

Public Finance.text: "Resource control" in the Nigerian federalism debate mainly refers to the demand by ____.
options: the federal government to take over all state revenues
private companies to be exempted from all taxes
oil-producing states for greater control over revenue derived from natural resources in their territory
foreign investors to own Nigerian land outright
Public Finance.correct_answer: oil-producing states for greater control over revenue derived from natural resources in their territory

Public Finance.text: The derivation principle in Nigeria's revenue allocation formula means that ____.
options: all revenue is shared equally regardless of origin
revenue is allocated based only on population size
revenue is allocated only to the federal government
a percentage of revenue is allocated to the state where the revenue, such as oil, was generated
Public Finance.correct_answer: a percentage of revenue is allocated to the state where the revenue, such as oil, was generated

Public Finance.text: Value Added Tax (VAT) revenue in Nigeria is an example of revenue that is ____.
options: collected by the federal government and shared among the three tiers of government
used exclusively to service external debt
Public Finance.correct_answer: collected by the federal government and shared among the three tiers of government

Public Finance.text: One argument in favour of a progressive tax system is that it ____.
options: encourages tax evasion among the poor
helps to reduce income inequality by taxing the rich at higher rates
places the heaviest burden on low-income earners
discourages government from providing public goods
Public Finance.correct_answer: helps to reduce income inequality by taxing the rich at higher rates

Public Finance.text: A key objective of public expenditure by government is to ____.
options: maximise the personal profit of government officials
eliminate all private sector economic activity
provide public goods and services that the private sector may under-provide
reduce the population of the country
Public Finance.correct_answer: provide public goods and services that the private sector may under-provide

Economic Growth and Development.text: Economic growth is best defined as ____.
options: a sustained increase in a country's real output (real GDP) over time
an improvement in the quality of life and welfare of citizens
a reduction in income inequality alone
an increase in the population of a country
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: a sustained increase in a country's real output (real GDP) over time

Economic Growth and Development.text: Economic development is a broader concept than economic growth because it includes ____.
options: only the increase in national output
improvements in living standards, health, education and reduction in poverty alongside increased output
only the increase in export earnings
only the growth of the manufacturing sector
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: improvements in living standards, health, education and reduction in poverty alongside increased output

Economic Growth and Development.text: Which of the following best distinguishes growth from development?
options: Growth is qualitative while development is quantitative
Growth and development mean exactly the same thing
Growth is a quantitative increase in output while development is a qualitative improvement in welfare
Growth only occurs in developed countries while development only occurs in developing countries
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: Growth is a quantitative increase in output while development is a qualitative improvement in welfare

Economic Growth and Development.text: A rise in a country's Gross Domestic Product over successive years, other things being equal, is an indicator of ____.
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: economic growth

Economic Growth and Development.text: The Human Development Index (HDI) combines indicators of ____.
options: life expectancy, education and income per capita
inflation rate, exchange rate and interest rate
import value, export value and trade balance
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: life expectancy, education and income per capita

Economic Growth and Development.text: A rising literacy rate in a country is generally regarded as an indicator of ____.
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: economic development

Economic Growth and Development.text: Life expectancy at birth, used as a development indicator, measures ____.
options: the average retirement age of workers
the number of years a person spends in school
the average number of years a newborn is expected to live given current mortality conditions
the total population of a country
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: the average number of years a newborn is expected to live given current mortality conditions

Economic Growth and Development.text: Which of the following is NOT typically used as an indicator of economic development?
options: The number of political parties in a country
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: The number of political parties in a country

Economic Growth and Development.text: Per capita income is calculated by dividing ____.
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: national income by total population

Economic Growth and Development.text: A fall in the infant mortality rate over time generally suggests ____.
options: an improvement in economic development and healthcare
an increase in the birth rate only
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: an improvement in economic development and healthcare

Economic Growth and Development.text: Which of the following is a major factor affecting a country's economic growth?
options: The number of public holidays in a year
The colour of the national currency
The quantity and quality of capital investment
The number of political parties registered
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: The quantity and quality of capital investment

Economic Growth and Development.text: Human capital, as a factor of economic growth and development, refers to ____.
options: the amount of money in circulation
the physical machinery used in factories
the land area of a country
the skills, knowledge and health of the workforce
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: the skills, knowledge and health of the workforce

Economic Growth and Development.text: Availability of natural resources can promote economic growth mainly because ____.
options: they provide raw materials for production and can generate export revenue
they automatically guarantee equal income distribution
they eliminate the need for capital investment
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: they provide raw materials for production and can generate export revenue

Economic Growth and Development.text: Technological progress contributes to economic growth chiefly by ____.
options: reducing the size of the labour force to zero
increasing productivity and efficiency in the production of goods and services
eliminating the need for natural resources
increasing the price of all goods automatically
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: increasing productivity and efficiency in the production of goods and services

Economic Growth and Development.text: A stable political environment favours economic growth and development because it ____.
options: encourages both local and foreign investment
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: encourages both local and foreign investment

Economic Growth and Development.text: Which of the following is a social/cultural factor that can hinder economic development?
options: Cultural practices and beliefs that discourage innovation and entrepreneurship
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: Cultural practices and beliefs that discourage innovation and entrepreneurship

Economic Growth and Development.text: The rate of capital formation (investment) in an economy directly affects economic growth because ____.
options: higher investment increases the productive capacity of the economy
investment has no effect on future output
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: higher investment increases the productive capacity of the economy

Economic Growth and Development.text: Which of the following is a major problem of economic development in Nigeria?
options: Too much diversification of the economy
Over-dependence on crude oil as the main source of foreign exchange earnings
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: Over-dependence on crude oil as the main source of foreign exchange earnings

Economic Growth and Development.text: Inadequate infrastructure, such as poor roads and unreliable electricity supply, is a major obstacle to development in Nigeria because it ____.
options: has no effect on the cost of doing business
raises the cost of production and discourages investment
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: raises the cost of production and discourages investment

Economic Growth and Development.text: High population growth rate can hinder economic development in Nigeria mainly by ____.
options: reducing the demand for education and healthcare
guaranteeing full employment for all citizens
outpacing the growth of resources and social amenities available per person
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: outpacing the growth of resources and social amenities available per person

Economic Growth and Development.text: Corruption is often identified as a major hindrance to Nigeria's economic development because it ____.
options: diverts public resources away from productive development projects
improves the efficiency of public institutions
has no effect on investor confidence
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: diverts public resources away from productive development projects

Economic Growth and Development.text: Low levels of capital formation in Nigeria are partly explained by ____.
options: an excessively high national savings rate
low savings due to widespread poverty and low income levels
abundant surplus capital with no use
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: low savings due to widespread poverty and low income levels

Economic Growth and Development.text: Political instability, such as frequent changes of government or civil unrest, hinders development mainly by ____.
options: discouraging both domestic and foreign investment due to uncertainty
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: discouraging both domestic and foreign investment due to uncertainty

Economic Growth and Development.text: The problem of capital flight in developing countries like Nigeria refers to ____.
options: the inflow of foreign capital into the country
the increase in domestic government spending
the rise in local manufacturing investment
the movement of large sums of money and investment out of the country to safer economies abroad
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: the movement of large sums of money and investment out of the country to safer economies abroad

Economic Growth and Development.text: Which of the following best describes the "brain drain" problem affecting Nigeria's development?
options: The emigration of skilled and educated citizens to other countries in search of better opportunities
The importation of foreign unskilled labourers
The migration of rural dwellers to urban areas within the country
The retirement of senior civil servants
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: The emigration of skilled and educated citizens to other countries in search of better opportunities

Economic Growth and Development.text: A narrow, undiversified export base is a development problem for Nigeria because ____.
options: it guarantees stable foreign exchange earnings at all times
it makes the economy highly vulnerable to fluctuations in the price of a single commodity like crude oil
it eliminates the need for economic planning
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: it makes the economy highly vulnerable to fluctuations in the price of a single commodity like crude oil

Economic Growth and Development.text: Development planning is best described as ____.
options: the random, unplanned actions of private individuals
a plan drawn up solely by foreign investors
a deliberate and coordinated government effort to achieve specific economic and social objectives over a period
a scheme with no defined targets or timeframe
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: a deliberate and coordinated government effort to achieve specific economic and social objectives over a period

Economic Growth and Development.text: One major objective of national development planning in Nigeria has been to ____.
options: increase dependence on a single export commodity
diversify the economy and reduce dependence on oil revenue
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: diversify the economy and reduce dependence on oil revenue

Economic Growth and Development.text: Nigeria's First National Development Plan was implemented during the period ____.
The Structural Adjustment Programme (SAP) introduced in Nigeria in 1986 was primarily aimed at ____.
options: increasing government control over all industries
restructuring and diversifying the economy away from oil dependence and reducing government's role in production
fixing the naira permanently to the US dollar at a high value
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: restructuring and diversifying the economy away from oil dependence and reducing government's role in production

Economic Growth and Development.text: Vision 2020, one of Nigeria's long-term development blueprints, aimed to make Nigeria ____.
options: completely dependent on agriculture alone by 2020
one of the top twenty economies in the world by the year 2020
a country with no private sector by 2020
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: one of the top twenty economies in the world by the year 2020

Economic Growth and Development.text: A key benefit of national development planning is that it helps to ____.
options: guarantee that resources are never scarce
eliminate the need for any government budget
coordinate the use of scarce national resources towards priority sectors
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: coordinate the use of scarce national resources towards priority sectors

Economic Growth and Development.text: One major challenge facing the successful implementation of development plans in Nigeria has been ____.
options: inadequate funding and poor project execution
excess availability of funds with no use
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: inadequate funding and poor project execution

Economic Growth and Development.text: The Millennium Development Goals (MDGs), later succeeded by the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), were global targets aimed mainly at ____.
options: reducing poverty, hunger, disease and inequality while promoting sustainable development
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: reducing poverty, hunger, disease and inequality while promoting sustainable development

Economic Growth and Development.text: Which of the following best describes "sustainable development"?
options: Development that maximises current consumption regardless of future consequences
Development that focuses only on industrial output
Development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: Development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs

Economic Growth and Development.text: A rise in unemployment despite a rise in GDP illustrates that ____.
options: growth and development always move together perfectly
unemployment always falls when GDP rises
GDP growth guarantees equal income distribution
economic growth does not always translate automatically into economic development for all citizens
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: economic growth does not always translate automatically into economic development for all citizens

Economic Growth and Development.text: Income inequality, even in a growing economy, is a development concern because ____.
options: the benefits of growth may not be shared fairly among the population
it guarantees that poverty will be eliminated
it has no effect on overall welfare
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: the benefits of growth may not be shared fairly among the population

Economic Growth and Development.text: Which of the following would most likely improve Nigeria's Human Development Index?
options: Reduced spending on schools and hospitals
Increased investment in education and healthcare
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: Increased investment in education and healthcare

Economic Growth and Development.text: The term "underdevelopment" typically describes an economy characterised by ____.
options: high technology, full industrialisation and high per capita income
a fully diversified and highly industrialised export base
low income, high poverty, low industrialisation and heavy reliance on primary production
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: low income, high poverty, low industrialisation and heavy reliance on primary production

Economic Growth and Development.text: Foreign direct investment (FDI) can promote economic growth and development in Nigeria by ____.
options: reducing the availability of jobs for citizens
automatically eliminating the need for local investment
bringing in capital, technology and employment opportunities
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: bringing in capital, technology and employment opportunities

Economic Growth and Development.text: A major reason economic planning is important for developing countries like Nigeria is that it helps to ____.
options: set clear priorities for the efficient allocation of limited resources over time
guarantee unlimited resources for every sector
remove the need for any government policy
ensure that all citizens have identical incomes instantly
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: set clear priorities for the efficient allocation of limited resources over time

Economic Growth and Development.text: Which of the following is an example of a social indicator, rather than a purely economic indicator, of development?
options: Literacy rate and access to healthcare
The exchange rate of the naira
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: Literacy rate and access to healthcare

Economic Growth and Development.text: A country can experience economic growth without economic development if ____.
options: rising output is matched by improved welfare for all citizens
poverty and inequality fall alongside rising output
rising national output is accompanied by worsening poverty, inequality and living conditions for most citizens
life expectancy and literacy rise alongside output
Economic Growth and Development.correct_answer: rising national output is accompanied by worsening poverty, inequality and living conditions for most citizens

Agriculture in Nigeria.text: Which type of farming is characterized by small-scale production mainly for family consumption rather than for sale?

Mechanized farming involves the use of which of the following?

options: Multiple food crops for local use

options: Farming scattered plots of different crops
Farming carried out only during the rainy season
Large-scale, single-crop cultivation often owned by companies

Agriculture in Nigeria.text: The role of agriculture in providing raw materials to industries is best illustrated by which example?
options: Iron ore supplied to steel mills

Agriculture in Nigeria.text: Agriculture contributes to Nigeria's economic development mainly by ____.
options: Reducing the need for foreign trade entirely
Providing employment for the majority of the rural population
Agriculture in Nigeria.correct_answer: Providing employment for the majority of the rural population

Agriculture in Nigeria.text: Before the discovery of oil, agriculture was Nigeria's major source of ____.

options: Industries buy all their raw materials from abroad
Farmers no longer need industrial products
Farmers consume manufactured inputs such as fertilizers and tools

Agriculture in Nigeria.text: Which of the following is a way agriculture aids capital formation in Nigeria?
options: Export earnings from cash crops can be reinvested in other sectors
Farmers hoard cash rather than invest
Agriculture in Nigeria.correct_answer: Export earnings from cash crops can be reinvested in other sectors

Agriculture in Nigeria.text: The system whereby land is inherited and fragmented among family members over generations, leading to small uneconomic farm sizes, describes a problem known as ____.
A major problem of Nigerian agriculture related to preserving harvested produce is ____.
Nigerian farmers often find it difficult to expand production because of ____.
Poor rural road networks affect Nigerian agriculture mainly by ____.
options: Making it difficult to transport produce to markets
Reducing the cost of farm inputs

Agriculture in Nigeria.text: Which of the following is a natural/biological problem affecting agricultural output in Nigeria?
The movement of able-bodied young people from farming communities to cities in search of white-collar jobs reduces the agricultural labour force. This movement is known as ____.
Farm holdings in Nigeria are often too small and scattered to allow efficient production, a problem referred to as ____.
The continued use of crude implements such as hoes and cutlasses by many Nigerian farmers is evidence of ____.
Inadequate irrigation facilities in Nigeria mean that farming is largely dependent on ____.
Unpredictable weather patterns and climate change affect Nigerian agriculture by causing ____.
Agricultural extension services are meant to ____.
options: Provide farmers with technical advice and new farming techniques
Agriculture in Nigeria.correct_answer: Provide farmers with technical advice and new farming techniques

Agriculture in Nigeria.text: The Nigerian government programme of the 1970s that encouraged citizens, including non-farmers, to engage in food production was called ____.
The 'Green Revolution' programme in Nigeria was primarily aimed at ____.
options: Reducing food imports through increased local agricultural production
Agriculture in Nigeria.correct_answer: Reducing food imports through increased local agricultural production

Agriculture in Nigeria.text: The Anchor Borrowers' Programme, introduced by the Central Bank of Nigeria, is designed to ____.
options: Provide farm inputs and credit linking smallholder farmers to processors
Agriculture in Nigeria.correct_answer: Provide farm inputs and credit linking smallholder farmers to processors

Agriculture in Nigeria.text: River Basin Development Authorities were established in Nigeria mainly to ____.
options: Manage water resources for irrigation and agricultural development
Agriculture in Nigeria.correct_answer: Manage water resources for irrigation and agricultural development

Agriculture in Nigeria.text: The National Fadama Development Programme in Nigeria focuses on ____.
options: Improving productivity of farmers in floodplain (fadama) areas
Agriculture in Nigeria.correct_answer: Improving productivity of farmers in floodplain (fadama) areas

Agriculture in Nigeria.text: A positive effect of well-implemented agricultural policies in Nigeria is ____.
options: Increased agricultural output and food security
Agriculture in Nigeria.correct_answer: Increased agricultural output and food security

Agriculture in Nigeria.text: Frequent changes in government agricultural policies in Nigeria tend to ____.
One of the major causes of instability of agricultural income in Nigeria is ____.
Fluctuations in world market prices for cash crops such as cocoa and rubber contribute to ____.
The seasonal nature of agricultural production, where crops are harvested only at certain times of the year, contributes to ____.
options: Elimination of the need for storage

Agriculture in Nigeria.text: Pest and disease outbreaks affecting crops or livestock can cause ____ in agricultural income.
One major effect of unstable agricultural income on farmers is ____.
options: Low and uncertain standard of living

Agriculture in Nigeria.text: Instability of agricultural income can lead to ____ as farmers seek more stable sources of livelihood.
Unstable agricultural income discourages ____ in the agricultural sector.

Crop insurance schemes help to reduce the effects of agricultural income instability by ____.
options: Increasing the price of farm produce artificially
Compensating farmers for losses due to natural disasters
Agriculture in Nigeria.correct_answer: Compensating farmers for losses due to natural disasters

Agriculture in Nigeria.text: Provision of irrigation facilities helps stabilize agricultural income mainly by ____.
options: Enabling farming throughout the year regardless of rainfall
Making farming dependent solely on rainfall
Agriculture in Nigeria.correct_answer: Enabling farming throughout the year regardless of rainfall

Agriculture in Nigeria.text: Encouraging farmers to grow a variety of crops rather than relying on a single crop, known as diversification, helps to ____.
options: Increase risk of total crop failure
Spread risk and stabilize farm income
Guarantee a single source of income
Agriculture in Nigeria.correct_answer: Spread risk and stabilize farm income

Agriculture in Nigeria.text: In Nigeria, the government body primarily responsible for agricultural policy formulation at the federal level is the ____.
options: Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development
